武利澤公司1853年由德國移民法蘭茲·魯道夫·武利澤在辛辛那提創立，初期進口弦樂: Wurlitzer was founded in Cincinnati in 1853 by the German immigrant Franz Rudolph Wurlitzer; at first it imported string, woodwind and brass instruments for resale, and it expanded later by supplying instruments to the US army. From 1880 it made pianos, moving to North Tonawanda in New York State and producing pipe organs, player pianos and theatre organs; the large theatre organs of the late 1910s became its signature product and were installed around the world. After the middle of the twentieth century the company turned to radios, jukeboxes, small electronic organs and portable electric pianos. In 1973 the jukebox business was sold to a German company, in 1988 the piano and organ brands were bought by Baldwin and later passed to Gibson; piano production ended in 2009 and jukebox production in 2013. In 2024 the brand brought out a new jukebox in partnership with a British manufacturer.
武利澤電鋼琴主要由木質琴體、金屬琴槌與弦組成。琴體採用優質硬木材料製造，提供穩定: The Wurlitzer electric piano consists mainly of a wooden body, metal hammers and strings. The body is made of good hardwood, giving a stable resonating chamber. The internal mechanism includes steel hammers, copper strings and adjusting rods, which keep the striking mechanism precise. The electronic amplification uses valve and transistor technology, with an aluminium or steel speaker frame. The keys are usually ivory or plastic, and the padding underneath is wool felt or leather, for feel and durability.
武利澤電鋼琴音色溫暖而獨特，兼具復古的機械質感與現代電子特徵。其高音域明亮靈動，: The Wurlitzer electric piano's timbre is warm and distinctive, with both a vintage mechanical feel and modern electronic features. The upper register is bright and lively with a clear penetration, while the middle and low registers are fuller and heavier, with a warm metallic sheen. Because it works by a mixture of mechanical and electric means, its timbre sits between the resonance of a traditional piano and the artificial quality of an electronic organ. Compared with a traditional piano the Wurlitzer electric piano is more buoyant; compared with a purely electronic organ it keeps more of the physical feel of hammers striking strings. Its resonance combines a mechanical action with electronic amplification, producing a particular depth of sound, and it suits jazz, rock and pop playing especially well.

魯道夫·武利澤公司（通常簡稱為武利澤公司）是一家美國公司，由德國移民（弗朗茲）魯: The Rudolph Wurlitzer Company (usually shortened to Wurlitzer) is an American company founded in Cincinnati in 1853 by the German immigrant (Franz) Rudolph Wurlitzer. At first the company imported string, woodwind and brass instruments from Germany for resale in the United States. Wurlitzer succeeded early on, thanks largely to defence contracts supplying instruments to the US military. In 1880 the company began making pianos, and eventually moved to North Tonawanda in New York State.
